about: isSupermodular is half of the hypothesis that makes g vanish, and the
implication as it was written is false.
The comment read: "RI <= 0 on every pair: then g == 0." On a total order
{x OR y, x AND y} is {x, y}, so RI is identically zero for every valuation.
The predicate cannot say no where it is used.
A vacuous predicate has no symptom. The only way to find one is to ask
whether it CAN disagree - which is what `vacuity.ts` does.
Neither half suffices alone. Among monotone valuations the converse holds:
`pricesAnything` carries both halves. `isSupermodular` stays: it tests the
raw RI condition, and on a total order RI really is identically zero.

coverage.criterion: the vacuity itself, on the structure production builds; a decreasing and a sawtooth valuation that are supermodular AND have a non-zero gap, which is the pair the old doc comment forbade; the increasing case, unchanged, so the repair is not an inversion; and both halves of the hypothesis failing alone on a non-chain

cases.name: the vacuity: on a chain, every valuation is supermodular
cases.why: on a total order {x|y, x&y} = {x, y}, so RI is identically 0

cases.name: THE COUNTEREXAMPLE: decreasing is supermodular and has a non-zero gap
cases.closed_form: g = min(u,w), which is exactly the 64 observed

cases.name: a second counterexample, non-monotone rather than reversed
the increasing case is unchanged: the repair is not an inversion
off the chain, supermodular ALONE licenses nothing
and monotone ALONE licenses nothing either — and the two agree exactly
